title: El calor
desc: You land, and the heat decides everything
spanish: greetings; ser vs estar for who you are and how you are; hace calor
nicaragua: Augusto C. Sandino airport; why Managua stops at midday; the dry season

title: Buenas
desc: One word does the work of ten
spanish: buenas / buenos dias / adios; usted vs vos as a first choice
nicaragua: Greeting everyone you pass, including strangers; not greeting is the rudest thing you can do
beat: You walk past three people in silence and feel the temperature drop.

title: Cordobas
desc: Money that is not yours yet
spanish: numbers 1-100; cuanto cuesta; pagar, costar, valer
nicaragua: The cordoba, called pesos in speech; why prices are said in tens
beat: You overpay a taxi four times over and only find out at dinner.

title: Gallo pinto
desc: Breakfast, and there is no other option
spanish: food nouns; me gusta as a first taste of gustar; querer + noun
nicaragua: Gallo pinto, cuajada, tortilla, tiste; the Nicaraguan breakfast table
beat: Dona Carmen feeds you before she asks your name.

title: El cuarto
desc: A room with a fan and no hot water
spanish: hay; there is / there is not; house vocabulary; prepositions of place
nicaragua: Renting a cuarto; nobody has hot water; the pila and what it is for
beat: You learn to bathe from a bowl and stop mentioning it.

title: Se fue la luz
desc: The power goes and nobody reacts
spanish: irse; the preterite of a handful of verbs, met whole, not explained
nicaragua: Power cuts as ordinary life; candles by the door; Disnorte
beat: The whole street carries on in the dark and you are the only one startled.

title: El agua
spanish: days of the week; time; tener que + infinitive
nicaragua: Water rationing; storing water; ENACAL; why the pila is always full
beat: You empty a barrel washing a shirt and learn what that costs.

title: Vos
spanish: voseo present of the verbs you already met: sos, tenes, queres, podes
nicaragua: Vos as the everyday form; usted for respect and distance; tu as foreign
beat: You say tu and a nine-year-old corrects you, kindly.

title: La pulperia
desc: The shop is somebody's front window
spanish: quantities; un poco, una bolsa, uno solo; dame / deme
nicaragua: Pulperias; buying one egg, one cigarette, one bag of water
beat: You discover you can buy anything in the smallest amount that exists.

title: Chele
desc: They have a name for you already
spanish: adjectives of description; ser + adjective; agreement
nicaragua: Chele and what it does and does not mean; nicknames by appearance
beat: Named by strangers, and deciding it is not an insult.

title: La fritanga
desc: Dinner comes off a grill on the sidewalk
spanish: ordering; quiero, deme, con, sin; food vocabulary widened
nicaragua: Fritanga; carne asada, maiz, tajadas, gallo pinto; eating standing up
beat: You order by pointing and it works perfectly.

title: Tengo hambre
spanish: tener hambre, sed, sueno, frio, calor, miedo, prisa
nicaragua: Why nobody lets a hungry person leave the house
beat: Hunger teaches you five expressions in one afternoon.

title: Los vecinos
desc: You have neighbours whether you want them or not
spanish: question words; the questions strangers ask; short answers
nicaragua: Dona and don; shared patios; children everywhere; why the questions are not intrusive
beat: In four minutes they know your age, your job and whether you are married.

title: El bus
desc: Getting on is the hard part
spanish: ir; a / para / hasta; giving and taking directions in one word
nicaragua: Rutas in Managua; the ayudante shouting the route; paying as you leave
beat: You take the wrong bus and it costs you an hour and nothing else.

title: Ideay
desc: Small words that carry a lot
spanish: ideay, dale, pues, va, fijate; the fillers that make speech sound Nica
nicaragua: How Nicaraguans actually punctuate a sentence out loud
beat: You use ideay correctly by accident and get a laugh.

title: La primera semana
spanish: recycling everything; the preterite of the week you just had
nicaragua: The shape of a Nicaraguan day, start to finish
beat: You realise you have not spoken English in three days.

title: Dos cuadras al lago
spanish: al lago, al sur, arriba, abajo; cuadras; landmarks as grammar
nicaragua: The Nicaraguan address system and why it works without street names
beat: You are given an address naming a tree that was cut down in 1998.

title: Donde fue el arbol
desc: Places that no longer exist are still directions
spanish: donde fue / donde estaba; imperfect met as a landmark, not a rule
nicaragua: Landmarks that are gone and still used; how everyone knows anyway
beat: You find the house. You still do not understand how.

title: Regateando
desc: Arguing about price without being rude
spanish: comparatives; mas barato, muy caro; conditional softeners
nicaragua: Where you bargain and where you never do; the rhythm of it
beat: You pay full price twice before somebody teaches you the dance.

title: La ruta 110
spanish: voseo imperatives: subite, bajate, agarrate, fijate
nicaragua: Managua rutas; interlocales to other cities; fare and etiquette
beat: An old woman offers you her seat and you have to refuse correctly.

title: El mototaxi
spanish: agreeing a price; cuanto me cobra; antes de + infinitive
nicaragua: Mototaxis and caponeras; settling the fare before you sit down
beat: You agree the price first. That is the entire lesson.

title: Un chip Claro
spanish: necesitar, servir, funcionar; numbers said aloud in long strings
nicaragua: Claro and Tigo; recargas at the pulperia; data as how people talk
beat: You learn six words about recharging because you have no choice.

title: El mercado Oriental
desc: The biggest market in Central America
spanish: clothing and household nouns; buscar, encontrar, perderse
nicaragua: How the Oriental is laid out; going with a list; going with somebody
beat: You get lost somewhere that has no map.

title: Vigoron
spanish: food widened; llevar, probar, servir; se sirve
nicaragua: Vigoron and Granada; yuca, chicharron, curtido; eating with your hands
beat: A day trip turns into a lesson taught by one dish.

title: Leon y Granada
desc: Two cities that do not like each other
spanish: comparisons between places; mas...que; opinions with creer
nicaragua: The Leon and Granada rivalry; liberal and conservative history in the streets
beat: Each city tells you the other one is arrogant.

title: El lago Cocibolca

nicaragua: Lake Cocibolca; Ometepe and its two volcanoes; the ferry from San Jorge

title: La epoca seca
desc: Two seasons, and this is the hard one
spanish: weather; hace / hay / esta; months; cuando + present
nicaragua: Dry season and green season; dust, burning, the first rain
beat: You finally understand why everyone talks about rain constantly.

title: En la ferreteria
spanish: describing an object you cannot name; para + infinitive; chunche, cosa
nicaragua: Hardware shops; chunche and cosa as universal nouns
beat: You do not know the word, so you describe it, and that turns out to be enough.

title: Los mangos
desc: Fruit falls on the roof for a month
spanish: fruit; too much / enough; demasiado, bastante, suficiente
nicaragua: Mango season; roadside fruit; green mango with salt and vinegar
beat: You are given more mangoes than one person can eat and cannot refuse.

title: El almuerzo
spanish: telling time loosely; a eso de; ya, todavia, ahorita
nicaragua: Comedorias; the buffet by pointing; why lunch is at noon and matters
beat: You eat at noon like everyone else and stop being hungry at odd hours.

title: Un mandado
spanish: favours; me hace un favor; ir a traer; poder + infinitive
nicaragua: How a mandado is not really a request, and why being asked is good news
beat: Dona Carmen sends you for tortillas, which means she trusts you.

title: El domingo
spanish: routines; reflexive verbs met whole; los domingos
nicaragua: Sunday: church, family, the beach, baseball; why nothing is open
beat: You try to do business on a Sunday and learn not to.

title: Pinolillo
desc: The drink the country is named after
spanish: drinks; hacer with recipes; se hace con
nicaragua: Pinolillo, tiste, cacao, chicha; why Nicaraguans call themselves pinoleros
beat: You are told that if you drink it you belong to them now.

title: Ya se llegar
spanish: giving directions yourself; imperatives recycled; saber + infinitive
nicaragua: Reading a city with no addresses; knowing your own barrio
beat: Somebody asks YOU for directions, and you answer without thinking.

title: Como te llamas de verdad
desc: Names, and all the ones you get given
spanish: llamarse; apodos; possessive adjectives
nicaragua: Nicknames for everyone; why your real name may never be used again
beat: You acquire a nickname and have no say in it.

title: La familia de Roberto
spanish: family vocabulary; de for relationships; tener + family
nicaragua: How wide a Nicaraguan family is; who counts as family
beat: You are introduced to eleven people and told they are all his brothers.

title: Pase adelante
desc: Being invited in, and not being able to refuse
spanish: formal imperatives with usted; pase, sientese, sirvase
nicaragua: Hospitality as obligation; why refusing food is refusing the person
beat: You say you are not hungry. It changes nothing at all.

title: Me cae bien
desc: Liking a person is a different verb
spanish: caer bien / mal; gustar-type verbs properly; indirect object pronouns
nicaragua: How Nicaraguans say they like somebody without saying it
beat: You say me gustas to a friend and learn the difference the hard way.

title: De donde sos
spanish: origin; ser de; nationalities; adjectives of place
nicaragua: What Nicaraguans want to know about your country and why
beat: You explain snow to somebody who has never been cold.

title: Contame
spanish: the preterite, properly this time; regular and the common irregulars
nicaragua: Storytelling as the main social currency; how a Nica tells a story
beat: You tell your first real story in Spanish and they laugh in the right place.

title: Ahorita
desc: A word that means four different things
spanish: ahorita, ya, ahora, al rato; time as intention rather than measurement
nicaragua: Why ahorita can mean now, soon, later, or never
beat: You wait two hours for an ahorita and learn to read the tone.

title: El cumpleanos
desc: A birthday, and you are expected
spanish: celebration vocabulary; felicidades; que cumplas muchos mas
nicaragua: Nicaraguan birthdays; the cake, the song, the mananitas, who pays
beat: You are handed the knife and do not know what that means.

title: Chavalos
desc: Children are everywhere and they are everyone's
spanish: diminutives; -ito and -ita as affection, not size
nicaragua: Chinear; how children move between houses; who disciplines whom
beat: A child you have never met falls asleep on you and nobody thinks it strange.

title: La iglesia
desc: Faith is not a private matter here
spanish: belief and hope; creer, esperar, rezar; si Dios quiere
nicaragua: Catholic and evangelical Nicaragua; primero Dios in ordinary speech
beat: You notice that every plan anyone makes has a condition attached to it.

title: El beisbol
spanish: sports; ganar, perder, jugar; team vocabulary
nicaragua: Baseball as the national sport; the Bosco, Dennis Martinez, the leagues
beat: You call it a strange choice and the room goes quiet.

title: Un favor
desc: Asking for something and owing something
spanish: polite requests; podrias, me hace el favor; conditional as courtesy
nicaragua: How favours circulate; why nobody keeps a ledger and everybody remembers
beat: You ask for help and immediately owe something you cannot name.

title: Que hiciste ayer
spanish: preterite in conversation; time markers; ayer, anoche, la semana pasada
nicaragua: What an ordinary Nicaraguan week actually contains
beat: You describe your week and realise it sounds like somebody else's.

title: Cuando era chavalo
desc: How people talk about the past that was ongoing
spanish: the imperfect; era, tenia, vivia; imperfect against preterite
nicaragua: Childhood in Nicaragua as it gets described; the countryside, the abuela
beat: Roberto tells you about growing up and you follow all of it.

title: La Gritería
desc: December 7, and the whole country shouts
spanish: call and response; que + noun; celebration vocabulary
nicaragua: La Purisima and La Griteria; Quien causa tanta alegria; altars, gorras, gofio
beat: You are pushed to the front of a doorway and told to shout the answer.

title: El mes de la patria
spanish: history vocabulary; dates; the preterite of historical events
nicaragua: September 14 and 15; San Jacinto; the torch from Guatemala; bandas de guerra
beat: A school parade closes your street for three hours and nobody minds.

title: Flores amarillas
desc: September 21, and you had better not forget
spanish: giving and receiving; regalar, dar, traer; para + person
nicaragua: Yellow flowers on the 21st; who gives them, who expects them, what it means
beat: You see every man on the street carrying the same flowers and understand you are late.

title: El dia de la madre
desc: May 30, and it is not negotiable
spanish: affection and respect; usted with your elders; querer vs amar
nicaragua: Mother's Day on May 30; why it outranks almost everything else in the year
beat: You learn the date exists, from somebody appalled that you did not know.

title: Vamos a la playa
desc: Making a plan with six people
spanish: future with ir a; suggestions; vamos, dale pues, nos vemos
nicaragua: Pochomil, Masachapa, Poneloya; how a Nicaraguan plan actually forms
beat: The plan changes four times and still happens.

title: Te presento a
spanish: presentations; mucho gusto, el gusto es mio; formal and informal registers
nicaragua: Who gets introduced first; the handshake, the kiss, the nod
beat: You get the order wrong and somebody quietly fixes it for you.

title: No seas malo
spanish: negative imperatives with vos; no seas, no digas, no te vayas
nicaragua: Vacilar; how affection is expressed as mockery here
beat: You are made fun of for an hour and slowly understand it is a welcome.

title: Salud
spanish: drinks; invitar; yo invito; rounds and who pays
nicaragua: Flor de Cana, Toña, Victoria; the guaro culture; who buys and when
beat: You try to pay separately and cause genuine offence.

title: Estoy enfermo
desc: Being ill somewhere you do not know the words
spanish: body parts; me duele; doler as another gustar-type verb
nicaragua: Farmacias, the doctor, home remedies, what an abuela prescribes
beat: Three different people give you three different cures and all are offended if refused.

title: Mi amigo
desc: When somebody stops being an acquaintance
spanish: friendship vocabulary; hermano, maje, broder as address
nicaragua: What maje means and who you can say it to; the line between friendly and rude
beat: Roberto calls you maje for the first time and it is a promotion.

title: Extraño mi casa
desc: Missing a place you chose to leave
spanish: extranar; emotions; estar + adjective; me siento
nicaragua: How Nicaraguans talk about the family members who left
beat: You admit you are homesick and get an answer you did not expect.

title: Ya sos de aqui
desc: The first time somebody says you belong
spanish: everything recycled; ser vs estar as identity vs state, revisited
nicaragua: What it takes to stop being a visitor
beat: Somebody introduces you as their friend and not as the chele.

title: Alquilando una casa
desc: Your own place, and a contract you half understand
spanish: housing vocabulary; conditions; si + present; deposito, alquiler, servicios
nicaragua: Renting without an agency; the handshake as the contract; what a landlord expects
beat: You agree to something you did not fully follow and it holds anyway.

title: El recibo
spanish: complaining politely; hay un error; deberia ser; conditional
nicaragua: Disnorte and ENACAL bills; how a Nicaraguan disputes one
beat: You are charged for a month you were not there.

title: Un tramite
desc: Paperwork, and the whole day gone
spanish: bureaucratic vocabulary; hay que, se necesita, falta
nicaragua: Migracion, the cedula, residencia; why you bring copies of everything twice
beat: You are sent home for a document nobody mentioned.

title: Otra vez manana
spanish: the subjunctive arrives: quiere que venga, necesito que traiga
nicaragua: Institutional time; how people cope; who you ask instead
beat: The third visit works, and you never learn why the first two did not.

title: Me cobraron de mas
spanish: standing your ground; eso no es lo que dijimos; past reference in argument
nicaragua: The chele price; how to close it down without making an enemy
beat: You push back for the first time and it works.

title: No estoy de acuerdo
spanish: opinion verbs; creo que, me parece que, la verdad es que
nicaragua: How disagreement is signalled here; the softeners that come first
beat: You disagree bluntly and watch it land badly.

title: Fijate que no
spanish: fijate que; indirect refusal; es que; the excuse as a form
nicaragua: Why a flat no is rude and what replaces it
beat: Somebody says yes to you for two weeks and means no the whole time.

title: Un trabajo
desc: Work, and what is expected of you
spanish: work vocabulary; schedules; obligation with tener que and deber
nicaragua: How work is found here; who recommends you; informality and its rules
beat: You are hired by somebody who never asks for a CV.

title: La quincena
desc: Money arrives twice a month and leaves faster
spanish: money verbs; ahorrar, gastar, prestar, deber; numbers in the thousands
nicaragua: The quincena; why everywhere is full on the 15th and the 30th
beat: You learn to shop on the right day of the month.

title: Me prestas
spanish: lending and borrowing; prestar vs pedir prestado; obligation and refusal
nicaragua: How lending works between friends and family; what is really being asked
beat: A friend asks and you do not know what saying no would cost.

title: El mecanico
desc: Something is broken and you cannot name it
spanish: describing faults; se descompuso, no sirve, hace un ruido raro
nicaragua: Talleres; fixing rather than replacing; the man who can fix anything
beat: You describe the noise with your mouth and he understands immediately.

title: Tuve un problema
spanish: preterite and imperfect together properly; narrating a mishap
nicaragua: How much detail a Nicaraguan story carries before the point arrives
beat: You tell it too fast and are made to start again.

title: Cuidado
desc: Safety, and how people talk about it
spanish: warnings; imperatives; no vayas, ten cuidado, mejor no
nicaragua: Which barrios, which hours, what people actually watch for
beat: You are warned off a street and take the warning seriously.

title: Me robaron
spanish: the passive se; se me perdio, se me cayo, me robaron
nicaragua: Reporting or not reporting; what people do instead
beat: You lose a phone and learn a grammar that puts the blame nowhere.

title: En el hospital
spanish: medical vocabulary; symptoms; the subjunctive after es necesario que
nicaragua: Public and private care; who waits with you; why nobody comes alone
beat: Four people you barely know sit in the corridor all night.

title: Que harias vos
spanish: the conditional properly; yo que vos; deberias
nicaragua: How advice is given here; why it arrives whether you asked or not
beat: You ask one person and end up with five opinions.

title: Es que no me entendiste
desc: A misunderstanding that becomes an argument
spanish: repair and clarification; lo que quise decir; no es eso
nicaragua: How a Nicaraguan de-escalates; the role of humour in stopping a fight
beat: You realise the argument is about something said three days ago.

title: Estoy arrecho
spanish: anger; arrecho, arrechera, molesto; intensity without insult
nicaragua: Arrecho as furious and as excellent; how the tone decides
beat: You use the word correctly and everyone stops talking.

title: Perdon
spanish: apology register; perdoname, disculpame, fue mi culpa, no fue mi intencion
nicaragua: What an apology has to contain here to actually count
beat: Your first apology is not accepted, and you learn what was missing.

title: Hablemos
spanish: nosotros commands; hablemos, veamos, dejemos; the subjunctive as invitation
nicaragua: Who initiates a hard conversation and where it happens
beat: You ask for the talk instead of waiting, and it goes better.

title: Prometiste
spanish: reproach; dijiste que, prometiste que; reported speech in the past
nicaragua: How seriously a spoken promise is taken; what excuses are accepted
beat: Somebody lets you down and you have to decide how much to say.

title: No es tan facil
spanish: listening; empathy phrases; te entiendo, que barbaro, que jodido
nicaragua: Economic reality most Nicaraguans live with; what is not said aloud
beat: You stop giving advice and just listen, which turns out to be the point.

title: Las remesas
desc: Money that crosses a border every month
spanish: sending and receiving; mandar, recibir, alcanzar; monthly obligation
nicaragua: Remittances from Costa Rica, the US, Spain; who is supporting whom
beat: You learn how much of the street is paid for from somewhere else.

title: Se fue para el sur
spanish: departure and absence; irse, quedarse, volver; future uncertainty
nicaragua: Migration to Costa Rica and beyond; the families left in the middle
beat: A friend leaves and the goodbye is deliberately small.

title: Aqui se hace asi
desc: Being corrected on how things are done
spanish: impersonal se; se hace, se dice, se usa; norms as grammar
nicaragua: The unwritten rules a foreigner keeps breaking
beat: You are told, kindly, that you have been doing something wrong for months.

title: Ya me defiendo
spanish: everything recycled in argument and negotiation
nicaragua: What competence looks like from the outside
beat: You sort out a problem alone that would have needed help in February.

title: La conoci
spanish: narrating a meeting; preterite and imperfect together; first impressions
nicaragua: Where people meet; the role of the group; who introduces whom
beat: An ordinary evening turns out later to have been the important one.

title: Me gusta ella
desc: Saying you like somebody, and getting it right
spanish: gustar with people; me gusta vs me cae bien vs la quiero
nicaragua: How interest is signalled here; what is direct and what is not
beat: You get the verb right this time and it is understood.

title: Una seña
spanish: indirect language; hints; parece que, creo que le gusto
nicaragua: Flirting as indirection; the role of friends as messengers
beat: Everybody around you knows before you do.

title: Salimos
spanish: invitations; te gustaria; conditional as courtship
nicaragua: What a date looks like; who pays; what time you bring her home
beat: You ask, badly, and she says yes anyway.

title: Mi amor
spanish: terms of endearment; mi amor, mi vida, mi cielo, mi reina
nicaragua: Why gordo and gorda are affectionate, and what happens if you assume otherwise
beat: She calls you gordo and you have to be told it is a good thing.

title: Chinearme
spanish: diminutives as affection; -ito, -ita on anything; chinear
nicaragua: How Nicaraguans express care physically and verbally
beat: You notice everything has become smaller: cafecito, ratito, amorcito.

title: Te quiero
desc: Querer and amar are not the same size
spanish: querer vs amar; degrees of declaration; when each is used
nicaragua: What is said early, what is saved, and what is never said aloud at all
beat: You say the bigger word first and she goes quiet.

title: Conoce a mi mama
spanish: usted as respect; formal register; mucho gusto, senora
nicaragua: What the mother is assessing; who you greet first; what you bring
beat: You are polite in the wrong register and she notices immediately.

title: La suegra
desc: The most important relationship you have now
spanish: deference; asking permission; le puedo, con su permiso
nicaragua: The suegra's authority; why the daughter's mother outranks you indefinitely
beat: You win one small point with her and it takes four months.

title: Los cuñados
spanish: banter; insults as affection; maje, no seas; teasing you can return
nicaragua: How brothers-in-law establish where you stand
beat: You are mocked for two hours and pass by not minding.

title: Que son tus intenciones
spanish: stating intent; pienso, quiero, voy a; future as commitment
nicaragua: When and how the question comes; who asks it
beat: Her father asks the question in front of everyone.

title: El dia de la madre
spanish: formal affection; congratulation; agradecer
nicaragua: Mother's Day on May 30; the serenata, the food, who cooks and who does not
beat: You understand for the first time how large this day is.

title: Flores amarillas
desc: The 21st, and you did not forget this year
spanish: giving; te traje, es para vos; anticipation and surprise
nicaragua: Yellow flowers on September 21; what it means to be remembered
beat: You are the one holding the flowers this time.

title: Estoy celoso
spanish: the subjunctive of emotion; me molesta que, no me gusta que
nicaragua: How jealousy is talked about here; what is normal and what is not
beat: You say the small true thing instead of the large false one.

title: No es lo que pensas
spanish: clarifying under pressure; no quise decir; entendiste mal
nicaragua: How a couple argues here; volume, and what volume does not mean
beat: You are shouted at and learn it is not the end of anything.

title: La plata
spanish: financial argument; alcanzar, gastar, hace falta; reproach
nicaragua: Whose money is whose; obligations to both families
beat: The argument is not about the amount and you both know it.

title: Tu familia o la mia
spanish: obligation and loyalty; tener que, deber, primero
nicaragua: Why her family's claim on her is not negotiable
beat: You ask her to choose and immediately wish you had not.

title: Perdoname
spanish: apology under real weight; me equivoque, tenes razon, no vuelvo a
nicaragua: What repair looks like; the gesture that goes with the words
beat: You apologise properly, and this one is accepted.

title: Hablemos de nosotros
desc: The conversation about what this is
spanish: the future; plans together; cuando + subjunctive
nicaragua: How couples here talk about the future; what is assumed rather than agreed
beat: You discover you had different timelines and neither had said so.

title: Se acabo
spanish: breaking up; ya no, se acabo, lo nuestro; the imperfect of what used to be
nicaragua: How an ending is handled; who is told, and in what order
beat: You use the past tense about a person for the first time.

title: Me duele
spanish: pain as an experience that happens to you; doler, extranar, faltar
nicaragua: Where you go, who feeds you, what the friends do
beat: Nobody asks if you want company. They just arrive.

title: Volvimos
spanish: reconciliation; volver a, otra vez, empezar de nuevo
nicaragua: Second chances and who has to speak first
beat: The making-up is quieter than the argument was.

title: Pedir la mano
spanish: formal request; quisiera, le pido, con todo respeto
nicaragua: Asking for her hand; who is present; what is served afterwards
beat: You rehearse a sentence for a week and say a different one.

title: La boda
spanish: ceremony vocabulary; vows; the subjunctive in wishes
nicaragua: Church and civil; padrinos; who pays for what; the hora nica
beat: It starts two hours late and nobody but you had expected otherwise.

title: Ahora somos familia
spanish: in-law vocabulary; suegro, cunado, concuno; belonging verbs
nicaragua: How you are addressed once you are family; what is now expected of you
beat: Her mother calls you mijo and you have to leave the room.

title: La casa poco a poco
spanish: progress over time; ir + gerund; poco a poco, ya casi
nicaragua: Building a house room by room over years; why nothing is finished
beat: You understand why so many houses have rebar sticking out of the roof.

title: El bautizo
desc: You are asked to be a godparent
spanish: acceptance and obligation; aceptar, comprometerse; formal thanks
nicaragua: Compadrazgo; what a padrino actually owes a child for life
beat: You say yes before understanding what you have agreed to.

title: Un chavalito
spanish: baby vocabulary; the language people use with infants; diminutives again
nicaragua: Who holds the baby, who visits, the forty days

nicaragua: Ruben Dario; why a poet is a national figure; what children memorise

nicaragua: Grandmothers as the source of authority in a disagreement

nicaragua: What Nicaraguan radio sounds like; the announcers, the adverts

nicaragua: Nicaraguan words that die at the border; what they cover

nicaragua: Seeing the country through new eyes again
